study_type.claude: Other (quantitative framework proposal with empirical validation; artifact mining)
study_type.note: Claude: quantitative framework proposal evaluated by regression and benchmarking on mined artifacts; NotebookLM: Mixed methods (counts the LLM text scoring as the qualitative strand). No human-subject qualitative data in the paper.

research_method.claude: Framework proposal (entropy-weighted indicator system + LLM semantic scoring + learnable fusion) evaluated by regression with industry fixed effects, benchmarking against baselines and heterogeneity analysis on mined development texts
research_method.nlm: Quantitative multi-dimensional indicator system with empirical regression/benchmarking plus LLM-based semantic scoring of textual artifacts
research_method.value: Framework proposal (LLM-EMM) with quantitative validation: entropy-weighted delivery/quality/collaboration indicator system fused with semantic scores from a fine-tuned LLaMA-3-8B (LoRA) over 380,412 textual artifacts; regressions of outcome variables on the fused scores, benchmarking against DORA, FPA, COCOMO II and expert scoring, sensitivity (fusion coefficient) and heterogeneity analyses by transformation stage and firm size
research_method.note: Industry fixed effects and robust s.e. reported only by Claude (not contradicted).

context.claude: Industry; 47 digitally transforming Chinese enterprises (fintech 18, smart manufacturing 15, e-commerce 14), 2021–2024; 380,412 artifacts (commit messages, code review comments, sprint retrospectives, incident reports)
context.nlm: Industry; 47 digitally transforming enterprises in China (fintech 18, smart manufacturing 15, e-commerce 14); 380,412 textual artifacts
context.value: industry; 47 digitally transforming enterprises in China (fintech 18, smart manufacturing 15, e-commerce 14); 380,412 textual development artifacts (commit messages, code review comments, sprint retrospectives, incident reports)

dora_applied.note: DORA used as structural scaffold of the delivery/quality sub-indicators ('DORA-derived sub-indicator groups') and also as a comparison baseline.

ai_discussed.note: LLM (fine-tuned LLaMA-3-8B) is the proposed measurement instrument; AI impact on developers is not evaluated.

remote_covid.note: Only a passing mention of 'geographically distributed team collaboration' in the introduction.

data_window.note: Claude: 2021–2024 (confirmed in text, Section 4); NotebookLM gives no period.

cat_productivity.note: Composite organizational efficiency index; FPA and COCOMO II effort as baselines.

cat_quality.note: Quality dimension (defect escape rate, defect density), post-release defect rate per KLOC.

cat_collaboration.note: Collaboration dimension of the indicator system; code review comments scored semantically.

cat_satisfaction.note: Only Customer Satisfaction Index (normalized NPS), i.e. customer satisfaction, not developer satisfaction.

cat_activity.note: Commit messages are scored for semantic content, not counted; NotebookLM's 'Activity' label on velocity stability does not fit the definition.

cat_delivery.note: Delivery dimension (deployment frequency) and release cycle compression outcome.

cat_agile.note: Team velocity stability (coefficient of variation of sprint velocity); sprint retrospectives among scored artifacts.

cat_survey.note: No developer perceptual instrument; NPS is a customer measure and expert scoring is only a weighting baseline.

evidence.quote: We conduct comprehensive empirical analysis on 47 digitally transforming enterprises across three industries, demonstrating consistent superiority over DORA, FPA, COCOMO, and expert scoring
we regress four organizational development outcome variables on the fused dimensional scores

The dataset comprises 47 digitally transforming enterprises in China (2021-2024) spanning fintech, smart manufacturing, and e-commerce sectors. A total of 380,412 unstructured textual artifacts were collected.
Inspired by the DORA framework and process-oriented quality models , we construct a hierarchical indicator system F that decomposes organizational efficiency into measurable atomic units.
directly corresponding to the three DORA-derived sub-indicator groups in Eq. (2).
In our implementation, L is instantiated as a fine-tuned LLaMA-3-8B (8 billion parameters, context window 8,192 tokens).
Let F = {D, Q, C} denote the three primary dimensions of our efficiency indicator space, where D represents the delivery dimension, Q the quality dimension, and C the collaboration dimension.
fusing structured and unstructured evidence into a unified composite efficiency index

Release Cycle Compression (Δτ, percentage reduction in average release cycle), Post-Release Defect Rate (ρ, defects per KLOC within 30 days), Team Velocity Stability (ζ , coefficient of variation of sprint velocity), and Customer Satisfaction Index (γ, normalized NPS).
